title: Pixel-Native RAG: A Practical Guide to Visual Document Indexing
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Move beyond traditional text-based parsing with PixelRAG, an end-to-end system that treats web pages and PDFs as images. This tutorial explores the complete pipeline—from rendering...
body:
Modelverse is excited to highlight a new, comprehensive tutorial on "Pixel-Native RAG," a groundbreaking approach to visual document indexing that moves beyond the limitations of traditional text-based retrieval. This innovative pipeline treats web pages and PDF documents as visual entities, sidestepping conventional HTML parsing, text extraction, and rigid chunking strategies. It offers developers and researchers a robust framework for building more resilient and accurate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, particularly for visually rich or complex content.

The core of Pixel-Native RAG involves rendering documents into images, which are then meticulously divided into overlapping tiles to preserve context. Multimodal embeddings are generated for these image tiles using advanced models like SigLIP, CLIP, or an optional Qwen3-VL backend, and subsequently stored in a FAISS index for efficient similarity search. To further enhance retrieval accuracy, the system incorporates OCR-based BM25 scoring for sparse retrieval, fusing these results with dense vector rankings via reciprocal rank fusion. An optional lightweight residual adapter can also be trained using contrastive learning to refine embedding quality.

This practical guide is invaluable for developers and researchers aiming to push the boundaries of RAG. It provides a complete, from-scratch implementation, including evaluation metrics and a FastAPI service for easy deployment and experimentation. By focusing on pixel-level understanding, Pixel-Native RAG offers a powerful solution for indexing diverse document types and directly feeding visual evidence to vision-language models for grounded answer generation, paving the way for truly multimodal AI applications.

title: SpaceX has bought $329M worth of Tesla Megapacks so far this year
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: The purchase illustrates just how interconnected Elon Musk's universe of companies are.
body:
### Recent Developments in AI Infrastructure
SpaceX has significantly increased its investment in Tesla's Megapack battery storage devices, spending a total of $329 million so far this year. This substantial purchase highlights the interconnectedness of Elon Musk's companies, with SpaceX and Tesla collaborating to support the growth of xAI, Musk's artificial intelligence business.

### Technology and Deployment
The Megapack batteries are likely being deployed at xAI's data centers to provide backup power and support the fluctuating energy demands of training AI models and running inference. These industrial-scale batteries play a critical role in smoothing out power peaks, reducing costs, and ensuring consistent data center operation. By leveraging the Megapack's capabilities, xAI can optimize its energy usage and minimize reliance on traditional power sources.

### Impact on Developers and Researchers
The integration of Megapack batteries into xAI's data centers has significant implications for developers and researchers working with AI models. By providing a stable and efficient power supply, these batteries enable the seamless training and deployment of AI models, driving innovation and advancement in the field. As xAI continues to expand its operations, the strategic deployment of Megapack batteries will be essential for supporting the growing demands of AI computing.
